newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb blast kills 21, wounds 60 in Algeria.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast kills 21, wounds 60 in Algeria.

text.p: A powerful bomb exploded on a bustling street in the centre of Algiers on Sunday evening, killing 21 people and wounding 60, the Algerian APS news agency reported.
The bomb, the second in the Algerian capital in 12 days, followed a massacre of villagers in Medea province, a stronghold of the feared Armed Islamic Group (GIA).
About 60,000 people have been killed in civil violence in Algeria since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election which radical Islamists were about to win.

"A bomb planted in a vehicle exploded around 2000 hours (2100 GMT) in Belouizdad avenue in Algiers. This new terrorist crime led to the killing of 21 people," APS said, quoting the Algerian security services.
The agency said the blast also injured 60 people, 30 of whom, including five in a grave state, were still being treated in hospital.

The bomb exploded during rush hour after people ended their daily fast during the Moslem month of Ramadan and one resident told Reuters by telphone from Algiers: "It was one of the most murderous blasts this year."

"Limbs of the victims, many of them hawkers in the street, were strewn on the pavement," said another resident. Emergency services rushed the scene to ferry the wounded to hospital and security forces sealed off the area.

One resident said the bomb was hidden in a bag and exploded near a crowded cafe and a cinema known as Cinema Musset. "Windows were shattered in many buildings nearby and some balconies collapsed," he said.
Interior Minister Mustapha Benmansour, who visited the scene to present his condolences to the families of victims, condemned what he described as "a criminal, cowardly and odious act," APS said.
He vowed "to hunt down and punish the perpetrators of the crime in Belouizdad neighbourhood, following the crime in Medea province."

Security forces reported earlier that 36 people were massacred in Sidi Abdelaziz village in Medea province, 70 km (40 miles) south of Algiers. They blamed the killings on a "group of terrorists", their term for anti-government Islamist guerrillas.

The massacre on Saturday night was the bloodiest in a series of killings, mostly in remote villages, and bombings in Algiers and surrounding towns which have claimed more than 300 lives in the past two-and-a-half months.
On Thursday, a bomb killed 14 people and wounded more than 100 in a crowded car market in Boufarik, 30 km (20 miles) south of Algiers.

Car bombs in Algiers and the eastern town of Ain-Fakroun killed 20 people 12 days ago and Moslem guerrillas slaughtered 14 villagers in Tabainat village, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers, a week ago.
The guerrillas have apparently stepped up their attacks during Ramadan, believing that the holy month is fitting for their "holy war" against the Algerian government.
